AA: the middle of the three conformance levels in the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
AAA: the highest of the three conformance levels in the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
AADT: annual average daily traffic, the vehicles a day a counting station records averaged over a year
ABN: Australian Business Number, the eleven-digit identifier the Australian Business Register issues
ACARA: Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority, which runs the My School website
ACN: Australian Company Number, the nine-digit identifier ASIC issues to a company
AEST: Australian Eastern Standard Time, ten hours ahead of UTC
AFP: Australian Federal Police, which also polices the Australian Capital Territory
AGPL: GNU Affero General Public License, the licence the site's code is under
AI: artificial intelligence, here the assistants and agents that read the site's files
AIHW: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare
API: application programming interface, an address a program reads data from
ASCII: the plain seven-bit character set, as in a file name with no accents or symbols
ASGS: Australian Statistical Geography Standard, the ABS boundaries such as SA2 and LGA
AU: Australia, as in the country code of a web address or a licence
BDM: Births, Deaths and Marriages, a state registry
BITRE: Bureau of Infrastructure and Transport Research Economics
BOCSAR: NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research
BPAY: the bill payment service run by Australian banks
CAAB: Codes for Australian Aquatic Biota, the CSIRO species code list
CC BY: Creative Commons Attribution, a licence that allows any use with credit to the publisher
CC BY-SA: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike, the Attribution licence with a condition that derived works use the same licence
CED: Commonwealth electoral division, a federal electorate
CKAN: the open-source data portal software most Australian government portals run
CSIRO: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation
CSV: comma-separated values, a plain-text table one row a line
CSVW: CSV on the Web, the W3C standard that describes a CSV file's columns
DCAT: Data Catalog Vocabulary, the W3C standard for describing datasets
DCCEEW: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, Australian Government
DEECA: Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action, Victoria
DETSI: Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation, Queensland
DISR: Department of Industry, Science and Resources, Australian Government
DOI: digital object identifier, a permanent reference for a published work
DPIRD: Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development, Western Australia
DTP: Department of Transport and Planning, Victoria
EPA: Environment Protection Authority, a state agency
EPSG: a coordinate reference system code from the register the European Petroleum Survey Group began
FDSV: family, domestic and sexual violence, an AIHW reporting program
FENICS: a market data provider whose overnight indexed swap rates the RBA quotes
FY: financial year, which in Australia runs from 1 July to 30 June
G-NAF: Geocoded National Address File, every Australian address with its coordinates
GDA2020: Geocentric Datum of Australia 2020, the coordinate reference frame Australian coordinates are published in
GDA94: Geocentric Datum of Australia 1994, the frame GDA2020 replaced
GLS: Government Licensing Service, the NSW licensing system the report is drawn from
GML: Geography Markup Language, an XML map file format
GNU: the free software project whose General Public License the site's code is under
GPS: Global Positioning System, the satellite system a receiver uses to work out where it is
HTML: the markup language of web pages
HTTP: the protocol a browser or program uses to fetch a web address
ICSEA: Index of Community Socio-Educational Advantage, the scale ACARA uses to compare the backgrounds of schools' students
IP: Internet Protocol, as in the address that identifies a device on the internet
ISO: International Organization for Standardization, as in the ISO 8601 date format
JSON: JavaScript Object Notation, a plain-text data format programs read
JSON-LD: JSON for Linking Data, the form of JSON that carries schema.org descriptions
KML: Keyhole Markup Language, a map file format
LGA: local government area, a council's boundary
MCP: Model Context Protocol, the standard an AI agent uses to call a server's tools
MMM: Modified Monash Model, the remoteness classification used for health workforce programs
NATA: National Association of Testing Authorities, which accredits laboratories
NDJSON: newline-delimited JSON, one JSON record a line
NHMD: National Hospital Morbidity Database, held by the AIHW
NHMP: National Homicide Monitoring Program, run by the Australian Institute of Criminology
NMD: National Mortality Database, held by the AIHW
OLGR: Office of Liquor and Gaming Regulation, Queensland
PCI: pulverised coal injection coal, a grade used in steelmaking
PM&C: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
PNG: Portable Network Graphics, an image format
POA: postal area, the ABS approximation of a postcode
PSMA: PSMA Australia, now Geoscape, which compiled G-NAF
Power BI: Microsoft's reporting tool, which reads a CSV from its address
RCV: Recorded Crime, Victims, the ABS series the AIHW tabulates
REST: representational state transfer, the style of web API that answers plain HTTP requests
SA2: Statistical Area Level 2, an ABS boundary of about 10,000 people
SA3: Statistical Area Level 3, an ABS boundary that groups SA2s
SA4: Statistical Area Level 4, the largest ABS sub-state boundary
SAL: suburb and locality, an ABS boundary
SED: state electoral division, a state electorate
SHA-256: a cryptographic hash, the fingerprint of a file's exact bytes
SQL: Structured Query Language, the language of database queries
TIFF: Tagged Image File Format, an image format also used for raster maps
TMR: Department of Transport and Main Roads, Queensland
TRAILS: Transport Registration and Integrated Licensing System, Queensland
TSV: tab-separated values, a plain-text table one row a line
UNSPSC: United Nations Standard Products and Services Code, a classification of what a contract buys
UTF-8: the Unicode text encoding every file here is written in
VGCCC: Victorian Gambling and Casino Control Commission
VS Code: Visual Studio Code, an editor that can connect to the MCP server
W3C: World Wide Web Consortium, the body that publishes web standards
WCAG: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international standard for accessible web content
WFS: Web Feature Service, a standard interface for fetching map features
WGS: World Geodetic System, the coordinate frame GPS uses
WGS84: World Geodetic System 1984, the coordinate frame GPS uses
WMS: Web Map Service, a standard interface for fetching map images
XML: Extensible Markup Language, a plain-text data format
YAML: the plain-text format the register's entries are written in
